newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says 33 climbers survived Andes avalanche.
newsitem.headline: Peru says 33 climbers survived Andes avalanche.

text.p: Rescue teams said on Tuesday that 33 mainly foreign climbers had survived unhurt from last Friday's massive avalanche on Peru's highest peak, Huascaran.
But Peruvian guide Cesar Henostroza and French climber Etienne Girard were assumed to have perished on the 22,127-foot (6,746 meter) mountain in northern Peru.
Their bodies are thought to be buried under 33 feet (10 meters) of snow.

"The majority of the climbers have been accounted for, but we continue the search for the missing Peruvian guide and the Frenchman," said Carlos Paredes, a civil defence spokesman in the nearby town of Huaraz. "Many days have passed already. I suspect they are dead."

The avalanche hit the hikers, most of them French, at a rest area known as Camp 2, some 19,352 feet (5,900 meters) on the southern slope of the snow-covered mountain in Peru's northern Ancash district.
The survivors managed to escape the crashing snow and make their way down the mountain.
Rescuers using helicopters and metal detectors were unable to find the two bodies. They did not believe anyone else was stranded.
Ancash, which includes the towering Cordillera Blanca or "White Range" of mountains, is one of Peru's most popular tourist regions.
